title: A generous act
tomorrow: a man reaches the altar, then walks away. why would Jesus say to?

lines: PAUL SAYS: NOT WHEN I COME.
cards: The card reader asks if you'd like to round up for charity, and there's one second to decide while the line waits behind you. That's generosity by ambush.
Fundraisers love a big moment: a speaker, a stage, a tally on the screen. So here's an odd detail.
Paul is collecting money for believers in need, and he tells a church in Corinth he wants no collection at all when he arrives. Why would a fundraiser skip his own big moment?

teach.b: Here's his plan, in the King James Bible: “Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.” Look inside that line.
A day: the first of the week.
A share: as God hath prospered him, in proportion to what came in, with no number given. And no scramble on arrival. In his next letter to the same church, Paul solves the puzzle himself.
He wanted the gift ready beforehand, so it would come as a willing gift and not something squeezed out under pressure.

teach.h: A CHEERFUL GIVER, A QUIET HAND.
teach.b: Then he says where the deciding happens: “Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.” Purposeth in his heart.
Planned, but not cold. The planning frees the gift from mood and moment, so it can be glad. Jesus adds how it's done: “But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.”
No announcement. A generous act can be money, but it can also be time, a meal, a ride, a skill. The pattern holds: chosen ahead, given gladly, kept quiet.

how: Some Christians set aside a planned amount each week or month for their church and for people in need, and some also plan one act of time or help each week, often given without telling anyone.

games.q: a charity gala asks for pledges live on stage, with a running tally on a big screen. your aunt asks how Paul handled giving in Corinth. what do you tell her?
o: he had it decided ahead, so it was ready and glad.
he saved the asking for when he arrived in person.
he set a fixed amount for each household to give.
games.why: Paul asked for weekly setting-aside so there be no gatherings when I come, and wanted the gift ready beforehand, willing rather than pressed.

practice: Decide one generous act for this week: what it is, who it's for, and when. Then name the likeliest thing to stop you, a busy day, a second thought, and the small move you'll make when it shows up.
Keep the whole plan between you and the person it's for.

wordCard.voice: A generous act. One gift a week, purposed in the heart ahead of time, given gladly, and kept quiet.

orig.note: Greek for cheerful, in God loveth a cheerful giver.

carryVoice: Keep this: planned generosity, decided before the moment, so the moment can be glad. Day 1703, given.
